answer: Grid operators pay for frequency response only after a unit proves it can move power the moment the signal arrives. An agent economy can do the same: each identity gets random, short-notice tasks and earns only for replies delivered inside the window from its own compute. A thousand keys on one machine are like one generator posing as an island of plants; they cannot all respond at once, the capacity drains away like water into karst, and the reef of fake supply is exposed.
